title: Segment vs Everyone
note: Computed by checks_dashboards_demo.py from the frozen .psv rows, with the same definitions truths.out uses. Each value carries the SQL it came from; Phase B2 holds every widget to these numbers.

kpis.label: AOV here
kpis.sql: SELECT round(avg(o.total_amount), 2) FROM dash_demo.orders o JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND g.country = 'Poland'

kpis.label: AOV everywhere
kpis.sql: SELECT round(avg(o.total_amount), 2) FROM dash_demo.orders o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'

kpis.label: Return rate here
kpis.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN 1 END) / count(*), 2) FROM dash_demo.orders o JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id WHERE true AND g.country = 'Poland'

kpis.label: Return rate everywhere
kpis.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN 1 END) / count(*), 2) FROM dash_demo.orders o

kpis.label: Largest category here
kpis.sql: SELECT pr.category FROM dash_demo.order_lines l JOIN dash_demo.orders o USING (order_id) JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id JOIN dash_demo.products pr USING (product_id) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND g.country = 'Poland' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY sum(l.line_amount) DESC LIMIT 1

kpis.label: Mobile app share of orders here
kpis.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN o.channel = 'mobile_app' THEN 1 END) / count(*), 2) FROM dash_demo.orders o JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id WHERE true AND g.country = 'Poland'

density.rule: a quarterly line for one segment needs 30 per quarter, which is why this demo is quarterly and not monthly
density.sql: SELECT min(n) FROM (SELECT count(*) AS n FROM dash_demo.orders o JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND g.country = 'Poland' GROUP BY date_trunc('quarter', o.order_ts))

density.bucket: country offered for comparison, orders in the whole period
density.rule: the select offers only countries with at least 400 orders (HAVING COUNT(*) >= 400)
density.sql: SELECT min(n) FROM (SELECT count(*) AS n FROM dash_demo.orders o JOIN dash_demo.geo_cities g ON g.city_id = o.city_id GROUP BY g.country HAVING count(*) >= 400)
